titre: The Binding of Isaac removes AI-generated music from new update

Developer Nicalis has removed AI-generated music that appeared in a new update for roguelike darling The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+. The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ received a new GTA 6-themed secret run this week, alongside the evergreen indie hit's PS5, Switch 2 and Xbox console ports, but players were quick to sniff out music generated with AI. Redditor ShweetsStuff found that the mode's new tracks were "100% generated with Suno (AI) (with proof)," by looking through "metadata included in the files shipped with the game." Player concerns were quickly confirmed by the game's original lead designer and Mewgenics co-creator Edmund McMillen. "Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he tweeted. It didn't take long for Nicalis to scrub the music in question from the game, either. Just yesterday, the studio pushed out a new update that removed "generated music files" on PC, alongside bug fixes and netcode improvements. The update has also been "submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo and Sony ASAP." There's no word on how exactly the genAI tracks slipped into the game. Nicalis is also "fixing compatibility that was inadvertently broken for the mod community (thanks for making cool stuff!)" Look forward to more in future updates, then. The controversy had a huge knock on effect to The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s Steam rating, as well. It now has an Overwhelmingly Negative rating on the platform, with just 8% of recent reviews logged as positive. "It's impressive that you can add nothing but crossplay in two years and somehow multiply the amount of bugs by three despite trying to fix those," one user review reads. titre: Binding of Isaac dev pulls AI-generated music from Repentance+ after players expose it
chapo: Nicalis has removed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac : Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest update, prompting a wave of negative reviews on Steam. Read more
extrait: Nicalis has removed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest update, prompting a wave of negative reviews on Steam. The music in question was tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6, which launched on the same day (19th November). A day later, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted that the run's music was "100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof)", pointing to tracks that reference the AI music tool Suno in their metadata. "Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one Steam review reads (thanks, IGN). "I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds [for] refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," said another. Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned. Responding to the criticism, Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen said he "woke up to a shit show". "Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he wrote on X/Twitter, before inviting players to report issues and bugs to the email address shared in one of Nicalis' tweets, which confirmed it had "pushed a new build with critical fixes", including the "removal of generated music files". The patch is live on PC, and Nicalis says it has been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony. Nicalis has yet to explain how the music ended up in the game. titre: The Binding of Isaac Dev Removes Undisclosed AI-Generated Music From Repentance+ Following Creator Response, Review-Bombing
chapo: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.
extrait: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen. McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity. "Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said. "I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said. "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful." The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6. What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch. As artificial intelligence advances, it's become increasingly difficult to discern human-made art from content pushed out by machines, but ShweetsStuff was able to provide evidence backing their claims. Specifically, they pointed to a handful of tracks that mention AI music software Suno in their metadata, which also included links to their Suno pages. AI-generated content passed off as art has already become controversial on its own in recent years. Adding to the fire for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was the fact that the music was featured in the new update without any sort of update to its Steam description. Valve requires developers to disclose how they may have used AI during game development, making the music's inclusion as puzzling as it is concerning for those who felt Nicalis had pulled the wool over their eyes. Negative reviews poured in following ShweetsStuff's discovery, leading McMillen to issue a statement today. He said he “had no idea" how AI-generated music found its way into the launch build of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s new update.
